subject: Maths
title: Compound interest and depreciation
subtitle: Percentages · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can calculate compound interest and depreciation using repeated percentage change.

key_vocab.definition: Compound interest is earned on the original amount AND on previous interest. Depreciation is when a value decreases by a fixed percentage each year.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can calculate compound interest and depreciation using repeated percentage change.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Compound interest and depreciation -- Compound interest is earned on the original amount AND on previous interest. Depreciation is when a value decreases by a fixed percentage each year.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Use the multiplier raised to the power of years. Growth: 1 + r. Depreciation: 1 - r.
A = P × (1 + r)n
P = principal, r = rate as decimal, n = years

Key examples:
  ✓ 5% increase: multiply by 1.05  (compound growth multiplier)
  ✓ 10% depreciation: multiply by 0.90  (depreciation multiplier)
  ✓ £1000 at 3% for 2 years = 1000 × 1.03²  (compound formula)
  ✗ 5% for 3 years = 15% total  (that is simple interest)
  ✗ 10% depreciation for 10 years = worthless  (it never reaches zero)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – compound interest
  £2000 is invested at 4% compound interest for 3 years. Find the final amount.
  Multiplier = 1 + 0.04 = 1.04
  A = 2000 × 1.04³
  A = 2000 × 1.124864 = £2249.73
  = £2249.73
  (Multiply by the growth multiplier for each year.)

Example 2 – finding interest earned
  £5000 at 3% compound interest for 2 years. How much interest is earned?
  A = 5000 × 1.03² = 5000 × 1.0609
  A = £5304.50
  Interest = 5304.50 - 5000 = £304.50
  = £304.50 interest
  (Subtract the original to find just the interest.)

sections.title: Compound interest
sections.content:
Find the final amount.

(a) £1000 at 5% for 2 years
(b) £3000 at 4% for 3 years
(c) £500 at 6% for 2 years
(d) £8000 at 2% for 4 years

sections.title: Interest earned
sections.content:
Find the interest earned (final amount minus principal).

(a) £2000 at 3% for 3 years
(b) £4500 at 5% for 2 years
(c) £10000 at 2.5% for 4 years
(d) £750 at 8% for 3 years

sections.title: Depreciation
sections.content:
Find the value after depreciation.

(a) £15000 car, 20% depreciation, 3 years
(b) £800 laptop, 25% depreciation, 2 years
(c) £6000 motorbike, 10% depreciation, 4 years
(d) £20000 van, 12% depreciation, 5 years

sections.title: Comparing simple and compound
sections.content:
Calculate both simple and compound interest, then find the difference.

(a) £1000 at 5% for 3 years: difference?
(b) £2000 at 4% for 4 years: difference?
(c) £5000 at 3% for 5 years: difference?
(d) £10000 at 6% for 3 years: difference?

sections.title: Mixed problems
sections.content:
Solve each compound percentage problem.

(a) £3000 invested at 4% for 5 years. Final amount?
(b) A phone worth £600 depreciates 30% yearly. Value after 3 years?
(c) Population 50000 grows 2% per year. Population after 10 years?
(d) £4000 grows to £4410 in 2 years. Annual rate?
(e) House worth £200000 increases 6% per year for 3 years. New value?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Compound interest grows faster than simple interest
✗ 5% compound interest for 3 years is 15% total increase
✓ Depreciation of 20% per year uses multiplier 0.8
✗ After 100% depreciation the item is worthless
✓ The compound interest formula is A = P(1 + r)^n
